_purpose: Functional scenarios (1 success + technique-driven alternative[]) per acceptance criterion for UC1b. No unit tests. Executable-ready — feeds test cases / automation.
_status: phase-3-3 output — 2026-07-09. Derived from PDT-3562-uc1b-complete-jira-story.json (AC+BR) + PDT-3562-uc1b-test-design.md (L3 conditions). UC1b = the 'Live' player component; the web-Live reveal-controls overlay + 1s auto-dismiss are NET-NEW (bare <video>+Plyr today) — most scenarios are 'Automate (when stable)'.

_rules_applied.split_per_state: No AC has >1 valid outcome by entry state → NO state splits; all 10 ACs → 1 scenario each. Desktop = 1-Step Pause (BR-09) and web-mobile-cannot-pause are PLATFORM variance → platform_expected on SC-UC1b-01/04/05, not a precondition-state split.
_rules_applied.one_owner_per_br: BR-01→AC-04 (SC-04) · BR-03→AC-03 (SC-03) · BR-06→AC-05 (SC-05) · BR-09→AC-01 (SC-01) · BR-10→AC-01 (SC-01) · BR-11→AC-04 (SC-04) · BR-15→AC-09 (SC-09). Each cross-cutting rule owned by the single most-direct AC; every other scenario cites (does NOT re-test). AC-01 owns BR-09+BR-10 (reveal-keeps-playing is the headline no-implicit-toggle); AC-04 owns BR-01+BR-11 (no-seek-on-Live + paused-persist).

scenarios.title: First tap on a playing 'Live' player reveals controls, playback continues (mobile)
preconditions: a 'Live' stream (SDK room_status=live) is actively playing on a mobile surface (iOS / Android / web-on-mobile)
the controls overlay is currently hidden
steps: Tap anywhere on the player surface (first tap)
Assert: the controls overlay appears
Assert: playback continues — the stream does not pause (video.paused === false)
Assert: the central button shows the PAUSE icon

expected.success: On mobile, the first tap reveals the controls overlay while the Live stream keeps playing (video.paused===false) and the central button shows the pause icon — the tap does not toggle playback.
alternative: The first tap must NOT pause the stream — a reveal that also toggles playback is the accidental-interrupt regression this story exists to prevent.
The overlay must actually appear — a first tap that neither reveals nor pauses (a no-op) is a failure.

platform_expected.note: Desktop = direct 1-Step Pause (BR-09): the first click PAUSES (video.paused===true) and shows the PLAY icon — the mobile reveal branch is not taken (TC-UC1b-04b)

scenarios.title: Tap outside the button (playing) dismisses the overlay, playback continues
preconditions: the controls overlay is visible over a playing 'Live' stream
the central pause/play button's rendered hit-target is 64x64px (FU-2 resolved)
steps: Tap the player surface outside the central button's 64x64px tap target
Assert: the overlay dismisses
Assert: playback continues — state stays playing (video.paused === false)

expected.success: Tapping outside the 64x64px central button dismisses the overlay while the Live stream keeps playing — the dismiss is not an implicit pause.
alternative: A tap-outside that transitions playing → paused is a failure — dismissing the overlay must never pause the stream (BR-10).

scenarios.title: No action for 1s (playing) auto-dismisses the overlay, playback continues
scenarios.automation_note: when-stable: web-Live net-new; web 3s->1s auto-dismiss regression guard
preconditions: the controls overlay is visible over a playing 'Live' stream
steps: Advance time to 999ms with no interaction; Assert: the overlay is STILL visible
Advance time to 1000ms; Assert: the overlay auto-dismisses
Assert: playback continues throughout — state stays playing

expected.success: After exactly 1s (1000ms) of no interaction while playing, the overlay auto-dismisses and playback continues; at 999ms it is still visible.
alternative: At 999ms (just before the 1s boundary) the overlay must still be visible — dismissing before 1s is a boundary failure.
The overlay must dismiss at 1000ms, not 3000ms — web currently uses a 3s timer (VideoPlayerControls.tsx:60-70); any dismiss later than 1s fails the regression guard.

scenarios.title: Pause a 'Live' stream: play icon persists, NO seek controls, tap-outside stays paused
preconditions: a 'Live' stream (mock SDK stream type = Live) is playing with the controls overlay visible
the central button's rendered hit-target is 64x64px (FU-2 resolved)
steps: Tap the central pause button
Assert: playback pauses (video.paused === true)
Assert: the icon switches pause->play and the PLAY icon remains visible
Assert: NEITHER the -10s NOR the +10s skip button is present in the view/DOM (a Live stream has no seek — BR-01)
Advance >1000ms with no interaction; Assert: the overlay PERSISTS (the paused branch has no idle auto-dismiss)
Tap outside the 64x64px central button; Assert: the overlay dismisses AND the stream stays paused (does not resume)

expected.success: On a Live stream the central pause tap pauses playback and the play icon persists; the ±10s seek buttons are never shown; while paused the overlay persists past 1s; a tap-outside dismisses it and the stream stays paused (resume-to-live is UC2).
alternative: Contrast: on a recorded / video stream the ±10s skip buttons ARE present — proving the seek gate is stream-type driven, not always-off (TC-UC1b-01c).
The paused overlay must NOT auto-dismiss on the 1s idle timer — a paused overlay that vanishes after 1s is a BR-11 failure.
A tap-outside while paused must never resume the stream — resume is out of scope here (UC2).

platform_expected.note: reaches the paused state via a 1-step pause (BR-09, TC-UC1b-04b) — there is no reveal-then-pause step
cannot pause a Live stream (platform table 68264) — reveal is in scope on web-mobile, pause is not; the pause assertions apply to iOS/Android

scenarios.title: Reveal / dismiss / auto-dismiss / pause behave identically across all in-scope surfaces
preconditions: a 'Live' stream renders on an in-scope surface (parameterize: inline feed, then fullscreen / gallery)
the platform is held fixed while the surface varies
steps: For surface = inline feed: run reveal (F02), tap-outside dismiss (F04), 1s auto-dismiss (F05), pause (F07); record the outcomes
For surface = fullscreen / gallery: run the same set; record the outcomes
Assert: the outcomes are IDENTICAL across the two surfaces

expected.success: The reveal / tap-outside-dismiss / 1s auto-dismiss / pause behaviours produce identical outcomes on the inline-feed and fullscreen/gallery surfaces (surface-invariant).
alternative: Any surface producing a DIFFERENT reveal, dismiss, auto-dismiss, or pause outcome than another in-scope surface is a surface-invariance break (BR-06 violation).

platform_expected.note: surface-invariant != platform-invariant: desktop still differs (1-Step Pause, BR-09) — that is expected platform variance, not a BR-06 break

scenarios.title: Default baseline — no controls overlay before the first tap
preconditions: SDK room_status = live and the post first renders
steps: Render the actively-playing Live post without any tap
Assert: no controls overlay element is present in the view hierarchy / DOM
Assert: the live video surface, the standing LIVE badge, and the viewer count are visible

expected.success: On first render of an actively-playing Live post with no tap, no controls overlay is present — only the live video surface, the standing LIVE badge, and the viewer count are visible (baseline S0).
alternative: The controls overlay must NOT be present before any tap — an overlay rendered pre-interaction is a baseline-state failure.

scenarios.title: Idle countdown restarts on every control interaction
preconditions: the controls overlay is visible over a playing 'Live' stream
steps: Interact with an overlay control at 800ms (before the 1s timeout)
Assert: the countdown restarts — the overlay is still visible at 1000ms after the original reveal
Take no further action; Assert: the overlay auto-dismisses 1000ms after the LAST interaction

expected.success: A control interaction at 800ms restarts the 1s countdown — the overlay stays visible past the original 1000ms and auto-dismisses only 1000ms after the last interaction.
alternative: If the overlay dismisses 1000ms after the FIRST reveal (ignoring the later interaction) the countdown-reset failed — the timer must restart on every control interaction.

scenarios.title: Pause tap races the auto-dismiss timer — explicit pause wins
scenarios.automation_note: when-stable: web-Live net-new; fake-timer race, component-level (real-time e2e timing is flaky)
preconditions: the controls overlay is visible over a playing 'Live' stream
the 1s idle auto-dismiss timer is about to fire (t≈1000ms)
steps: Dispatch a central pause-button tap at t=1000ms — the exact instant the auto-dismiss would fire (fake-timer race)
Assert: the explicit pause WINS — state becomes paused (video.paused === true)
Assert: the PLAY icon is shown and persists (not swallowed by the expiring timer)
Assert: the overlay dismisses only on a subsequent tap-outside, not from the fired timer

expected.success: When the pause tap lands at the exact instant the 1s auto-dismiss fires, the explicit pause wins: state becomes paused, the play icon persists, and the overlay is not swallowed by the expiring timer — it dismisses only on a later tap-outside.
alternative: The expiring timer must not swallow the pause — a race where the overlay auto-dismisses and the paused / play-icon state is lost (or the stream stays playing) is the failure mode.

scenarios.title: Tap during buffering surfaces the real state — no false 'playing' icon
scenarios.automation_note: with-mock: SDK buffering / route stall + throttle
preconditions: a 'Live' stream is buffering (not yet playing) — SDK state = buffering (mock), or forced via route stall + network throttle
steps: Tap the player surface while buffering
Assert: the controls overlay appears
Assert: the central button reflects the REAL (buffering) state — NOT a false 'playing' pause-icon
Assert: no crash and no frozen overlay

expected.success: Tapping the player while the Live stream is buffering reveals the overlay with the central button reflecting the real buffering state — never a false 'playing' pause-icon — with no crash and no frozen overlay.
alternative: [AI-INFERRED] Mid-play stall (was playing, then the network stalls): an explicit buffering / 'Reconnecting' state must surface — the viewer is never left on a silent frozen frame (BR-15). Extends AC-09 initial-buffer to a mid-play stall per BR-15 'any interruption' (web gate isLoading && isPoorConnection && isLive; iOS scrim+spinner); paused-reconnect is UC2.
The central button must never show a false 'playing' pause-icon while the stream is buffering — the state must reflect reality.

scenarios.title: App backgrounded during an active overlay/timer reaches a well-defined state (OS default)
scenarios.automation_note: when-stable: web-Live net-new; OS-default bg/fg — Detox bg/fg + real-device confirm (web has no visibilitychange handler); Live snap-to-live = UC2 (not asserted)
preconditions: the controls overlay is visible with the idle timer active over a playing 'Live' stream
the app is then backgrounded for >1s
steps: Background the app for >1s, then return it to the foreground
Assert: the player / overlay reach a well-defined state via the OS default (Option 1) — no stale mid-countdown overlay
Assert: no implicit play/pause toggle beyond the OS default

expected.success: Backgrounding the app for >1s while the overlay/timer is active and returning to foreground yields a well-defined state via the OS default — no stale mid-countdown overlay and no implicit play/pause toggle beyond the OS default.
alternative: A stale mid-countdown overlay left on screen after foreground, or an implicit play/pause toggle beyond the OS default, is the failure mode.
Live foreground snap-to-live is UC2's behaviour — observed here, never asserted.
